content.text: {"decision":"YES","supporting_policy_ids":["E01","E02","E03","E04","E05","E06","E07","E08","E09","E10","E11","E12","E13"],"decisive_condition_ids":["a1","a2","a3","a4","a5","a6","a7","a8","a9"],"unresolved_condition_ids":[],"missing_facts":[],"justification":"All nine conditions for Gift Aid eligibility are satisfied for donation FP-0316-EL from Elaine Carter on 16 March 2026. (a1) The charity holds confirmed HMRC recognition as of that date. (a2) The donation was made by a named individual from her own bank account. (a3) Elaine paid £980 in Income Tax for 2025–26, which exceeds the £80 total Gift Aid being claimed on her donations that year, satisfying the tax-paid threshold. (a4) A signed Gift Aid declaration covering this specific payment exists. (a5) The donation was not made through Payroll Giving. (a6) No goods or services were exchanged. (a7) Elaine received no benefit in exchange. (a8) The donation was not a transfer of shares. (a9) FP-0316-EL was a direct bank transfer, explicitly distinguished from CAF voucher or charity-card payments. All exclusions under E08–E13 are inapplicable. Therefore, a Gift Aid claim can be made on this donation, entitling the charity to claim 25p per £1 donated (i.e. 25% of £120 = £30). Note: other donors and transactions in the scenario have not been assessed here and would each require individual evaluation.","scope_issues":["This determination covers only donation FP-0316-EL from Elaine Carter.
